resources.string: Shows when SmartEQ Pro is actively processing system audio
Universal mode active — equalizing all streaming media and downloaded files system-wide.
Legacy mode active — applying to the device\'s global audio output.

"Default mode listens for a signal that well-behaved apps (like most music and podcast players) send when they start or stop playing audio, and attaches the equalizer to that specific app. It\'s the mode Google currently recommends and generally sounds identical to Legacy mode, with better battery life.\n\nLegacy mode instead attaches the equalizer to the phone\'s entire audio output at once. It can pick up audio from apps that don\'t send the signal Default mode listens for, but Google has marked this approach as outdated, and a small number of phones (mostly certain Samsung and Xiaomi models) don\'t allow it at all. If Default mode isn\'t picking up your audio, try Legacy mode — SmartEQ Pro will tell you plainly if it isn\'t working on your device."

"Typing an artist, song, or genre into 'Intelligent Auto-EQ' can be handled two ways:

• Without an API key: SmartEQ Pro uses its own built-in library of hand-tuned artist and genre profiles. This works fully offline-capable for network use — no data leaves your device for this feature.

• With a Google Gemini API key: the app asks Gemini to generate a custom curve for exactly what you typed, which can be more precise for artists not in the built-in library. This sends the artist/song name and your headphone model to Google's Gemini API over an encrypted connection.

This is entirely optional. Nothing about the core equalizer, presets, or Auto-Tune requires it."

"Connecting Spotify lets SmartEQ Pro read what track is currently playing (song title, artist, album art) so it can automatically suggest or apply a matching EQ preset. It does not let SmartEQ Pro control playback, see your password, or access anything beyond what's currently playing and your playlists.

SmartEQ Pro does not receive Spotify's actual audio stream through this connection — if you want SmartEQ Pro to equalize Spotify's sound, that happens separately through the system-wide equalizer engine (see 'How system-wide processing works'), which works whether or not you connect a Spotify account.

You can disconnect at any time in Settings; this immediately deletes the stored access token from this device."

"SmartEQ Pro uses Android\'s built-in audio effects framework to insert your equalizer and dynamics settings into the audio path of other apps while they play — the same official mechanism used by other system-wide EQ apps. It does not record, capture, or store any audio content, and does not need microphone access to do this.\n\nCompatibility varies by source app and phone manufacturer, which is a limitation of Android itself rather than of this app. The status indicator on the Equalizer screen always tells you honestly whether a compatible session was found."

"App Lock requires your fingerprint, face, or device PIN/pattern/password before SmartEQ Pro opens or returns from the background. It protects your saved presets and, if connected, your Spotify session from anyone else with access to your unlocked phone. SmartEQ Pro never sees or stores your biometric data itself — Android handles that matching privately and only tells the app pass or fail."

"Bass and Treble apply a broad tonal tilt below ~150 Hz and above ~8 kHz. The Dynamics section (Threshold, Ratio, Attack, Release, Knee) is a compressor: it automatically narrows the gap between the quietest and loudest parts of what you\'re listening to. Lower thresholds and higher ratios compress harder; Attack/Release control how quickly it reacts."
Optional — leave blank to use the built-in local tuning library
Use your fingerprint, face, or device PIN
SmartEQ Pro must show a persistent notification while the equalizer engine is running — this is an Android requirement for any app that processes audio continuously, not optional tracking.
